answer: Privacy-preserving personhood checks work by letting several independent issuers each confirm a person unique, without sharing raw data. Each issuer gives the person one blinded token, and the network accepts only identities holding tokens from three different issuers. Like timber from separate forests, no single supplier can flood the system, and cheating issuers lose their status. A sonnet follows strict rules, and so does this scheme: fixed formats, public lists, revocation for abuse. The forge stays cold, because faking an identity would require corrupting three issuers at once.
